This analysis repeats Analysis 7's comparison of StimGate, F-beta and Tailgate
when the stimulation causes no response at all. The true background-subtracted
frequency is then zero, so every non-zero estimate is an error, and a method
should report a frequency close to zero rather than find a response.

## Set-up

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(furrr)
library(progressr)

root_dir <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("DESCRIPTION")) "." else "..", winslash = "/")
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root_dir, "DESCRIPTION")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root_dir)

scripts_r_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "r")
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-runtime.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-plot-style.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-mcse.R"))
analysis_qmd <- "analysis/7b-sim-compare-null.qmd"

run_simulations <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_simulations",
  "RUN_SIMULATIONS",
  FALSE
))
analysis_run_id <- .get_qmd_param_env(
  "analysis_run_id",
  "ANALYSIS_RUN_ID",
  NULL
)
analysis_key <- c("sim", "compare", "null")
simulation_seed <- as.integer(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "simulation_seed",
  "SIMULATION_SEED",
  12345L
))
if (is.na(simulation_seed)) {
  stop("simulation_seed must be coercible to an integer.")
}
comparison_semantics_version <- "compare-null-v2"
analysis_dev <- .analysis_is_dev()
analysis_quick <- .analysis_is_quick() && !analysis_dev
# "draft" (current default) or "final" sample/dataset counts; dev and quick win.
sim_size <- .analysis_sim_size()
analysis_key <- .analysis_mode_key(analysis_key)
fig_key <- .analysis_mode_key("7b-sim-compare-null")
run_plots <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_plots",
  "RUN_PLOTS",
  TRUE
))
# Monte Carlo error bars on the summary plots (see analysis-mcse.R).
mcse_mode <- .analysis_mcse_mode(.get_qmd_param_env("show_mcse", "SHOW_MCSE", "on"))
show_mcse <- mcse_mode != "off"
sim_grid_chunk_index <- as.integer(
  .get_qmd_param_env("sim_grid_chunk_index", "SIM_GRID_CHUNK_INDEX", 1L)
)
sim_grid_n_chunks <- as.integer(
  .get_qmd_param_env("sim_grid_n_chunks", "SIM_GRID_N_CHUNKS", 1L)
)
.validate_sim_grid_chunk_settings(sim_grid_chunk_index, sim_grid_n_chunks)
sim_chunk_label <- .sim_chunk_label(sim_grid_chunk_index, sim_grid_n_chunks)

desc_path <- file.path(root_dir, "DESCRIPTION")

if (
  file.exists(desc_path) &&
    grepl("Package: stimgate", readLines(desc_path, n = 1))
) {
  devtools::load_all(root_dir)
} else {
  stop("Expected the stimgate DESCRIPTION at the repository root: ", root_dir)
}

if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_require_packages(c("simcyto", "scales"))
}

if (isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  .analysis_require_packages(c("cytoUtils", "openCyto", "flowStats", "simcyto"))
}

# Source simulation helpers in dependency order:
# 1. sim-misc.R: general simulation utilities and transformation lookups
# 2. sim-bandwidth.R: location details reader and bandwidth helpers
# 3. sim-compare-freq_bs.R: comparison functions requiring the helpers above
# 4. sim-compare-null.R: this analysis's grid, summaries and figures
for (fn in c(
  "sim-misc.R",
  "sim-bandwidth.R",
  "sim-bandwidth-analysis-io.R",
  "sim-bandwidth-analysis-plot.R",
  "acs_cytof-plot_cyt.R",
  "sim-compare-freq_bs.R",
  "sim-compare-detection.R",
  "sim-compare-null.R"
)) {
  source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, fn))
}

```

## Scientific settings

### Aim

Analysis 7 measures how well each method estimates a response that is there.
Here no cell responds: the stimulated tube is drawn from the same distribution
as the unstimulated tube. Two situations are covered:

1. Neither tube has any cytokine-positive cells: both are all negative cells.
2. Both tubes have the same share of cytokine-positive (background) cells,
   either low (0.01%) or higher (1%). The positive cells follow the same
   distribution as Analysis 7's responding cells, so they look like a response
   in each tube on its own, but they are no more common in the stimulated tube.

Every method setting is Analysis 7's (see that analysis for the reasons):
StimGate with automatic `nrd0` bandwidths shared per marker, its unstimulated
bias equal to the shared bandwidth, threshold clustering and the capped
local-FDR threshold method; Tailgate with automatic tolerance and a bias of
0.15; F-beta with the standard settings. Tailgate without the bias ("Tailgate
(default settings)") is kept in the tables.

### Simulation settings

As in Analysis 7, each scenario simulates 20 datasets of 20 samples in final
runs and 5 datasets of 20 samples in draft runs (`SIM_SIZE=draft`), the samples
of a dataset are gated together, and the dataset is the unit for uncertainty.
The cell counts, transformations and separations (positions of the positive
cells) are Analysis 7's. Cell counts are exact (`probExact = TRUE`), so both
tubes have the same number of positive cells and the true net frequency is
exactly zero. Scenarios that would duplicate another are left out: with no
positive cells the separation does nothing, so only one separation is run, and
a 0.01% background rounds to no cells at 1,000 and 5,000 cells per tube, so it
is run only at 20,000 (2 positive cells per tube) and 100,000 (10).

```{r}
#| label: actual-settings
n_cell_stim_vec <- c(1e3, 5e3, 2e4, 1e5)
# No response; the background share of positive cells is the same in both tubes.
prob_background_vec <- .simCompareNullBackgrounds

mean_pos_settings_tbl <- .simMiscGetMeanPosTbl()

transformation_vec <- c("gaussian", "gamma", "skew")
sample_perturbation_sd_vec <- 0
condition_perturbation_sd_vec <- 0
cluster_perturbation_sd_vec <- 0
n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim_vec <- 1

# StimGate bandwidth settings.
stimgate_bw_mtd <- "nrd0"
stimgate_bw_scope <- "cytokine"
# StimGate's unstimulated-sample bias equals its shared bandwidth:
# with biasUns = NULL, gateStim() uses bwShared * biasUnsFactor.
stimgate_bias_uns_factor <- 1
stimgate_bw_ncell_max <- 1e4
# Tubes with fewer cells are upsampled to this many before bandwidth selection.
stimgate_bw_ncell_min <- 1e4
stimgate_bw_fallback <- "auto"
stimgate_bw_min <- "none"
stimgate_bw_max <- "none"

# StimGate method settings for the full method comparison.
# Cluster refinement is enabled to represent the full one-marker procedure.
# Share thresholds across clusters of similar samples via stimControl(clusterGates = ).
cluster_gates <- TRUE
loc_enforce_shape_threshold <- FALSE
# Condition-level local-FDR gate: the region boundary, moved up only where
# its frequency exceeds 1.3 times the probability-sum estimate ("cap").
stimgate_loc_threshold_method <- "cap"
calc_cyt_pos_gates <- FALSE
# Each dataset of `n_sample_sim` samples is gated together (shared settings
# and cluster gates), so the dataset is the unit for uncertainty. Draft keeps
# the samples per dataset and uses a quarter of the datasets (at least 5).
n_sample_sim <- if (analysis_quick) 1L else 20L
n_iter_sim <- if (analysis_quick) 1L else c(final = 20L, draft = 5L)[[sim_size]]

fbeta_beta <- 0.8
fbeta_theta <- 2
fbeta_width <- 10
path_fbeta <- file.path(
  root_dir,
  "scripts",
  "python",
  "fbeta.py"
)
if (isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  if (!file.exists(path_fbeta)) {
    stop("F-beta comparison script not found: ", path_fbeta)
  }
  .simCompareFbetaEnvironment(pathFbeta = path_fbeta)
}

tailgate_adjust <- 1
tailgate_method <- "firstDeriv"
tailgate_tol <- 1e-2
tailgate_auto_tol <- TRUE
# Tailgate's cutpoint is moved up by this amount, as StimGate's gates are
# moved up by its bias. The unbiased cutpoint is kept as "tailgate_default".
tailgate_bias <- 0.15
tailgate_x <- "stim"
```

## Simulation

Each biological scenario has its own seed, assigned on the full grid before
quick/dev filters or chunking. Each replicate dataset has a seed drawn before
any method runs.

### Simulation grid

```{r}
#| label: compare-grid
#| include: false
sim_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  mean_pos_settings_tbl,
  prob_response = 0,
  prob_background = prob_background_vec,
  n_cell = n_cell_stim_vec,
  bw_mtd = stimgate_bw_mtd,
  bw_scope = stimgate_bw_scope,
  bw_ncell_max = stimgate_bw_ncell_max,
  bw_ncell_min = stimgate_bw_ncell_min,
  bw_fallback = stimgate_bw_fallback,
  bw_min = stimgate_bw_min,
  bw_max = stimgate_bw_max,
  sample_perturbation_sd = sample_perturbation_sd_vec,
  condition_perturbation_sd = condition_perturbation_sd_vec,
  cluster_perturbation_sd = cluster_perturbation_sd_vec,
  n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim = n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim_vec
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bias_uns = NA_real_,
    bias_uns_factor = stimgate_bias_uns_factor
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    transformation,
    prob_response,
    prob_background,
    n_cell,
    mean_pos_setting,
    mean_pos,
    bw_mtd,
    bw_scope,
    bw_ncell_max,
    bw_ncell_min,
    bw_fallback,
    bw_min,
    bw_max,
    bias_uns,
    bias_uns_factor,
    sample_perturbation_sd,
    condition_perturbation_sd,
    cluster_perturbation_sd,
    n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim
  ) |>
  # Drop duplicates: separation is irrelevant without positive cells, and a
  # background that rounds to no cells is the no-background scenario.
  dplyr::filter(
    !(prob_background == 0 & mean_pos_setting != "high"),
    !(prob_background > 0 & round(n_cell * prob_background) < 1)
  ) |>
  .simCompareNullSeedGrid(simulation_seed)

# Keep every seeded row available for an exact interactive rerun.
sim_grid_full <- sim_grid

# Quick mode: smallest grid covering every figure; dev takes precedence.
if (analysis_quick) {
  sim_grid <- sim_grid |>
    dplyr::filter(
      n_cell %in% c(5e3, 2e4),
      transformation %in% c("gaussian", "gamma"),
      mean_pos_setting == "high"
    )
}

if (analysis_dev) {
  sim_grid <- sim_grid |>
    dplyr::filter(
      n_cell == 2e4,
      prob_background == 1e-2,
      mean_pos_setting == "high",
      transformation == "gaussian"
    )
}

sim_grid_all <- sim_grid
analysis_grid_spec <- sim_grid_all

if (sim_grid_n_chunks > 1L && nrow(sim_grid_all) > 0L) {
  sim_grid <- sim_grid_all |>
    dplyr::filter(
      ((dplyr::row_number() - 1L) %% sim_grid_n_chunks) + 1L ==
        sim_grid_chunk_index
    )
}

sim_grid
print(paste0("Total simulation scenarios: ", nrow(sim_grid)))
```

Run the simulations in parallel, with progress reporting. Each scenario has a
deterministic seed recorded in `sim_seed`, so its simulation is stable
across worker scheduling and grid chunking.

```{r}
#| label: compare-parallel
#| include: false
n_workers <- max(1, .simGetCores())

analysis_result_params <- list(
  comparison_semantics_version = comparison_semantics_version,
  simulation_seed = simulation_seed,
  analysis_grid_spec = analysis_grid_spec,
  analysis_quick = analysis_quick,
  analysis_dev = analysis_dev,
  sim_size = sim_size,
  n_cell_stim_vec = n_cell_stim_vec,
  prob_response = 0,
  prob_background_vec = prob_background_vec,
  transformation_vec = transformation_vec,
  mean_pos_settings_tbl = mean_pos_settings_tbl,
  sample_perturbation_sd_vec = sample_perturbation_sd_vec,
  condition_perturbation_sd_vec = condition_perturbation_sd_vec,
  cluster_perturbation_sd_vec = cluster_perturbation_sd_vec,
  n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim_vec = n_cell_uns_relative_to_stim_vec,
  stimgate_bias_uns_factor = stimgate_bias_uns_factor,
  prob_exact = TRUE,
  cov_ev_min = 1.5,
  cov_ev_max = 1.5,
  n_sample_sim = n_sample_sim,
  n_iter_sim = n_iter_sim,
  stimgate_bw_mtd = stimgate_bw_mtd,
  stimgate_bw_scope = stimgate_bw_scope,
  stimgate_bw_ncell_max = stimgate_bw_ncell_max,
  stimgate_bw_ncell_min = stimgate_bw_ncell_min,
  stimgate_bw_fallback = stimgate_bw_fallback,
  stimgate_bw_min = stimgate_bw_min,
  stimgate_bw_max = stimgate_bw_max,
  cluster_gates = cluster_gates,
  loc_enforce_shape_threshold = loc_enforce_shape_threshold,
  stimgate_loc_threshold_method = stimgate_loc_threshold_method,
  calc_cyt_pos_gates = calc_cyt_pos_gates,
  fbeta_beta = fbeta_beta,
  fbeta_theta = fbeta_theta,
  fbeta_width = fbeta_width,
  tailgate_adjust = tailgate_adjust,
  tailgate_method = tailgate_method,
  tailgate_tol = tailgate_tol,
  tailgate_auto_tol = tailgate_auto_tol,
  tailgate_bias = tailgate_bias,
  tailgate_x = tailgate_x
)


compare_raw <- tibble::tibble()

if (isTRUE(run_simulations)) {
  run_ctx <- .analysis_run_context(
    analysis_key = analysis_key,
    run_id = analysis_run_id,
    qmd_path = analysis_qmd,
    path_root = root_dir,
    params = c(
      list(
        run_simulations = run_simulations,
        run_plots = run_plots,
        sim_grid_chunk_index = sim_grid_chunk_index,
        sim_grid_n_chunks = sim_grid_n_chunks
      ),
      analysis_result_params
    ),
    sim_grid_chunk_index = sim_grid_chunk_index,
    sim_grid_n_chunks = sim_grid_n_chunks
  )

  path_progress_file <- run_ctx$progress_file
  dir_output <- run_ctx$chunk_output_dir
  dir.create(dir_output, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(dirname(path_progress_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  path_rds <- file.path(
    run_ctx$staging_collated_dir,
    if (sim_grid_n_chunks > 1L) {
      sprintf("compare_raw_chunk_%s.rds", sim_chunk_label)
    } else {
      "compare_raw.rds"
    }
  )

  if (interactive()) {
    progressr::handlers(global = TRUE)
  }

  if (nrow(sim_grid) > 0L) {
    compare_raw <- .simCompareFreqBsGrid(
      sim_grid = sim_grid,
      nSample = n_sample_sim,
      nIter = n_iter_sim,
      nMarker = 1,
      nCondition = 2,
      nCluster = 2,
      probExact = TRUE,
      covEvMin = 1.5,
      covEvMax = 1.5,
      clusterGates = cluster_gates,
      locEnforceShapeThreshold = loc_enforce_shape_threshold,
      locThresholdMethod = stimgate_loc_threshold_method,
      calcCytPosGates = calc_cyt_pos_gates,
      pathFbeta = path_fbeta,
      fbetaBeta = fbeta_beta,
      fbetaTheta = fbeta_theta,
      fbetaWidth = fbeta_width,
      tailgateAdjust = tailgate_adjust,
      tailgateAutoTol = tailgate_auto_tol,
      tailgateBias = tailgate_bias,
      tailgateMethod = tailgate_method,
      tailgateTol = tailgate_tol,
      tailgateX = tailgate_x,
      parallel = (n_workers > 1L),
      workers = n_workers,
      dirCache = dir_output,
      pathProgress = path_progress_file,
      dirJobs = run_ctx$chunk_jobs_dir,
      progressHeading = "NULL-RESPONSE COMPARISON SIMULATION PROGRESS",
      resume = TRUE,
      retryErrors = TRUE,
      sim_grid_chunk_index = if (sim_grid_n_chunks > 1L) {
        sim_grid_chunk_index
      } else {
        NULL
      },
      sim_grid_n_chunks = if (sim_grid_n_chunks > 1L) {
        sim_grid_n_chunks
      } else {
        NULL
      }
    )

    .write_rds_atomic(compare_raw, path_rds)
  } else {
    message("No simulations assigned to this chunk.")
  }

  chunk_check <- .simCompareGridOutputStatus(
    compare_raw,
    sim_grid = sim_grid,
    nSample = n_sample_sim,
    nIter = n_iter_sim
  )
  chunk_collate_ok <- isTRUE(chunk_check$collate_ok)
  chunk_validation_ok <- isTRUE(chunk_check$validation_ok)
  n_failed <- length(chunk_check$failed_ids)
  n_completed <- length(chunk_check$completed_ids)

  validation_error <- if (!chunk_collate_ok) {
    paste0(
      "Chunk collation does not match the assigned simulation grid. Missing sim_id: ",
      paste(chunk_check$missing_ids, collapse = ", "),
      "; extra sim_id: ",
      paste(chunk_check$extra_ids, collapse = ", "),
      "."
    )
  } else if (length(chunk_check$failed_ids) > 0L) {
    paste0(
      "Chunk contains incomplete, non-finite or errored primary method results for sim_id: ",
      paste(chunk_check$failed_ids, collapse = ", "),
      "."
    )
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  .analysis_mark_chunk(
    run_ctx = run_ctx,
    total_sims = nrow(sim_grid),
    completed_sims = n_completed,
    failed_sims = n_failed,
    collate_ok = chunk_collate_ok,
    validation_ok = chunk_validation_ok,
    error_message = validation_error
  )

  if (!isTRUE(chunk_validation_ok)) {
    stop(validation_error)
  }

  .simComparePromoteIfReady(
    run_ctx = run_ctx,
    sim_grid_all = sim_grid_all,
    total_sims = nrow(sim_grid),
    completed_sims = n_completed,
    failed_sims = n_failed,
    nSample = n_sample_sim,
    nIter = n_iter_sim
  )

  if (sim_grid_n_chunks > 1L) {
    message(
      "Completed this simulation chunk. ",
      "Render with run_simulations = FALSE after all chunks are promoted ",
      "to inspect summaries or write plots."
    )
    knitr::knit_exit()
  }
} else {
  run_ctx <- .analysis_results_context(
    analysis_key = analysis_key,
    path_root = root_dir,
    qmd_path = analysis_qmd
  )
  message("Skipping simulations; using canonical promoted results.")
}
```

## Collation

```{r}
#| label: compare-collate
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# Without `run_ctx` (simulation chunk not run in this session), read the
# canonical promoted results under `current/`.
if (!exists("run_ctx")) {
  run_ctx <- .analysis_results_context(
    analysis_key = analysis_key, path_root = root_dir, qmd_path = analysis_qmd
  )
}

path_rds <- .analysis_current_file(
  run_ctx = run_ctx,
  relative_path = c("collated", "compare_raw.rds"),
  required_params = analysis_result_params
)
compare_raw <- .analysis_read_rds(path_rds, analysis_key, analysis_qmd)

if (any(compare_raw$propRespTruth[compare_raw$method %in% .simCompareMethods] != 0)) {
  stop("Every simulated net frequency must be exactly zero in this analysis.")
}
null_scores <- .simCompareFisherScores(compare_raw)
null_errors <- .simCompareNullErrors(null_scores)
scenario_cols <- c("transformation", "mean_pos_setting", "mean_pos",
  "prob_background", "n_cell", "method")
null_summary <- .simCompareNullSummary(null_errors, scenario_cols,
  mcse = show_mcse && isTRUE(run_plots))
null_detection <- .simCompareDetectionSummary(null_scores, scenario_cols,
  mcse = show_mcse && isTRUE(run_plots))
null_evidence <- .simCompareEvidenceSummary(null_scores, scenario_cols,
  mcse = show_mcse && isTRUE(run_plots))
null_provenance <- .simCompareNullProvenance(null_errors,
  setdiff(scenario_cols, "method"))

if (!isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  message("run_plots is false, so stopping after collation.")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}

if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(null_summary,
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "null-error-summary.csv"),
    "Signed and absolute frequency errors (percentage points) by scenario and method.",
    path_root = root_dir)
}
plot_dir <- .analysis_fig_dir(fig_key, path_root = root_dir)
```

## Results

The error is the estimated background-subtracted frequency minus the true
one, which is zero. Signed estimates are displayed as percentages: 0.01% is
one extra positive cell per 10,000 in the stimulated tube. Absolute errors
are in percentage points. `error_pp` already includes the factor of 100;
figures do not rescale it again. Negative net estimates remain negative. Statistics pool every
sample of every dataset in a scenario (tube-level distributions). With Monte
Carlo intervals on (`show_mcse`), error bars are 95% bootstrap intervals that
resample whole datasets, so they reflect the datasets, not the tubes, as the
independent unit; at least five datasets and 95% finite bootstrap draws are
required. Comparator runtime errors are missing outcomes, not zero errors;
`n_finite` in the summary table counts the samples with an estimate.

Figures show StimGate, F-beta and Tailgate (with its bias); Tailgate at its
default settings is in the CSV tables only. Panels have their own y ranges.
Without positive cells there is no separation setting, so those figures have
one panel per transformation.

```{r}
#| label: null-figures
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
fig_methods <- c("stimgate", "fbeta", "tailgate")
fig_specs <- list(
  list(stat = "error_median", name = "median_error",
    heading = "Median error",
    text = "The median signed error: a typical sample's estimate.",
    y = "Estimated net response (%)", zero = TRUE),
  list(stat = "error_p90", name = "p90_error",
    heading = "90th percentile of the error",
    text = paste("The 90th percentile of the signed error: one sample in ten",
      "overestimates by more than this (an apparent response)."),
    y = "90th percentile of estimated net response (%)", zero = TRUE),
  list(stat = "abs_error_p90", name = "p90_abs_error",
    heading = "90th percentile of the absolute error",
    text = paste("The 90th percentile of the absolute error, in either",
      "direction: one sample in ten is further from zero than this."),
    y = "90th percentile of absolute response error (percentage points)", zero = FALSE)
)
for (bg in prob_background_vec) {
  .analysis_heading(.simCompareNullBackgroundLabel(bg), 3L)
  d_bg <- null_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(prob_background == bg, method %in% fig_methods)
  for (spec in fig_specs) {
    .analysis_heading(spec$heading, 4L)
    cat(spec$text, "\n\n")
    .analysis_print_save_fig(
      .simCompareNullPlot(d_bg, spec$stat, spec$y, zero_line = spec$zero,
        by_separation = bg > 0),
      file.path(plot_dir, spec$name,
        paste0("null_", spec$name, "_background_", format(bg, scientific = TRUE), ".png")),
      width = 20, height = 22, mcse_mode = mcse_mode
    )
  }
}
```

### Share of samples with a positive estimate

A positive estimate is an apparent response. Shares are over the samples
with an estimate, by scenario and method.

```{r}
#| label: null-share-positive
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(
    null_summary |>
      dplyr::select(transformation, mean_pos_setting, prob_background, n_cell,
        method, n_sample, n_finite, share_positive) |>
      dplyr::mutate(share_positive = round(share_positive, 3)),
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "null-share-positive.csv"),
    "Share of samples with a positive estimated frequency.", path_root = root_dir)
}
```

### How StimGate set its gates

StimGate can report that it found no response: its local-FDR step then
returns no threshold and a fallback gate is used. The table counts, per
scenario, samples whose gate came from local FDR directly, from another
sample through threshold sharing, or from a fallback.

```{r}
#| label: null-provenance
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(null_provenance,
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "stimgate-gate-provenance.csv"),
    "StimGate gate provenance by scenario (samples).", path_root = root_dir)
}
```

## Detection evidence under the null

For each sample and method, the one-sided Fisher exact test asks whether the
final gated-positive proportion is greater in the stimulated tube. The 2×2
table contains positive and negative counts from each tube; cells are not paired.
The saved final applied-gate counts are used, with no re-gating. Log upper-tail
probabilities preserve very small p-values even when the ordinary p-value
underflows. Errored gates and missing estimates are missing tests.

A detection requires a positive estimated net response **and** p ≤ alpha.
Under these simulated null scenarios the detection rate is an empirical
false-positive rate, not a false discovery rate. The denominator is samples
with valid estimates and count tables. Coverage, missing estimates and bootstrap
validity are exported separately. Intervals resample whole datasets, preserving
paired method results, using the same eligibility rules as the frequency figures.

```{r}
#| label: null-detection
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(null_scores,
    c(fig_key, "null-sample-evidence.csv"),
    "Saved counts and uncapped Fisher/SBB evidence for every sample and method.", path_root = root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(null_detection,
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "null-detection.csv"),
    "Empirical false-positive rates and valid/missing sample coverage.", path_root = root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(dplyr::filter(null_detection, abs(alpha - 0.05) < 1e-12),
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "null-detection-alpha-005.csv"),
    "False-positive rates at the conventional 0.05 cutoff, by scenario and method.", path_root = root_dir)
  for (bg in prob_background_vec) {
    for (sep in unique(null_detection$mean_pos_setting[null_detection$prob_background == bg])) {
      .analysis_heading(paste(.simCompareNullBackgroundLabel(bg), sep, "separation"), 3L)
      d <- dplyr::filter(null_detection, prob_background == bg,
        mean_pos_setting == sep, method %in% fig_methods, alpha >= 0.001, alpha <= 0.2)
      .analysis_print_save_fig(.simCompareNullDetectionPlot(d),
        file.path(plot_dir, "detection", paste0("fpr_background_", bg, "_", sep, ".png")),
        mcse_mode = mcse_mode, fit_panels = TRUE)
    }
  }
}
```

### Exploratory heat maps at alpha = 0.05

These compact views use a common 0–100% colour scale and print each rate.
Grey NA tiles distinguish unrun or unavailable scenarios from zero detections.
Each separation has its own figure; no-background scenarios appear only at
high separation because the other separations were not simulated.

```{r}
#| label: null-detection-heatmap
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  for (sep in unique(null_detection$mean_pos_setting)) {
    .analysis_heading(paste(sep, "separation"), 4L)
    .analysis_print_save_fig(.simCompareNullDetectionHeatmap(
      dplyr::filter(null_detection, mean_pos_setting == sep, method %in% fig_methods)),
      file.path(plot_dir, "detection_heatmap", paste0("fpr_005_", sep, ".png")),
      width = 20, height = 16)
  }
}
```

### Evidence scales

The base-10 Fisher scale is the primary view; base-2 is a companion with the
same ordering. The [Sellke, Bayarri and Berger (2001) calibration](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~berger/papers/99-13.html)
uses B01_min = −e p log(p) for p < 1/e, and 1 otherwise. It is a lower bound
on the Bayes factor favouring a precise null; −log10(B01_min) is an upper
bound on log Bayes-factor evidence against that null, **not** an estimated or
exact Bayes factor. Fisher p-values after adaptive gating are not guaranteed
to be calibrated. Discreteness also differs from the continuous-null calibration
assumptions, so the Berger transformation is exploratory until calibration
has been established.

Summaries are computed from uncapped scores. Display caps start at 12 on the
base-10 Fisher scale, with corresponding caps on the other scales. Hollow upward
triangles mark capped summaries; CSVs include the number of individual samples
above the cap, even if their median or 90th percentile is below it. Dotted lines
mark nominal p = 0.05. No testing family size is specified for this one-marker
simulation, so no Bonferroni threshold is invented.

```{r}
#| label: null-evidence
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(null_evidence,
    c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "null-evidence-summary.csv"),
    "Uncapped evidence quantiles, cap exceedances and bootstrap coverage.", path_root = root_dir)
  evidence_labels <- c(fisher_log10 = "Fisher evidence: −log10(p)",
    fisher_log2 = "Fisher evidence: −log2(p)",
    sbb_log10 = "Exploratory upper bound: −log10(B01_min)")
  for (score in names(evidence_labels)) {
    .analysis_heading(evidence_labels[[score]], 3L)
    for (bg in prob_background_vec) {
      .analysis_heading(.simCompareNullBackgroundLabel(bg), 4L)
      for (stat in c("median", "p90")) {
        .analysis_heading(if (stat == "median") "Median" else "90th percentile", 5L)
        d <- dplyr::filter(null_evidence, prob_background == bg, method %in% fig_methods)
        .analysis_print_save_fig(.simCompareNullPlot(d, paste0(score, "_", stat),
          paste(if (stat == "median") "Median" else "90th percentile of", evidence_labels[[score]]),
          zero_line = FALSE, by_separation = bg > 0,
          display_cap = .simCompareEvidenceCap(score), reference = .simCompareEvidenceReference(score)),
          file.path(plot_dir, "evidence", score, paste0(stat, "_background_", bg, ".png")),
          mcse_mode = mcse_mode, fit_panels = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Detection sensitivity versus empirical false-positive rate

Analysis 7 uses background = 0.2 × response probability; Analysis 7b uses
absolute backgrounds of 0, 0.01% and 1%. Only response 0.05% in Analysis 7
matches a requested background (0.01%). Matching also requires the same
transformation, separation, parent-cell count, perturbations, tube-size ratio
and realised unstimulated background frequency. Realised zero responses are
excluded from sensitivity. The source grid allows comparisons at 20k and 100k;
the 0.01% null grid intentionally omits 1k and 5k. Quick/dev reductions can
leave no matched scenarios. Other response magnitudes remain unmatched.

Both analyses use the same positive-net-response rule and Fisher cutoffs.
ROC-style points are empirical estimates, with independent dataset resampling
between analyses and shared resampling across methods within each analysis.
The 5% table selects the largest *simulated* cutoff whose observed FPR is at
most 5%, only when thresholds bracket 5%. It reports the attained FPR and
sensitivity, not interpolated sensitivity at exactly 5%. Missing brackets and
large gaps remain limitations. Bootstrap intervals at a selected cutoff are
pointwise; they do not include cutoff-selection uncertainty.

```{r}
#| label: null-response-roc
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  response_cache <- tryCatch({
    response_ctx <- .analysis_results_context(.analysis_mode_key(c("sim", "compare", "freq_bs")),
      path_root = root_dir, qmd_path = "analysis/7-sim-compare-freq_bs.qmd")
    response_manifest <- .analysis_read_manifest(file.path(response_ctx$current_dir, "manifest.rds"))
    source_params <- .simCompareDetectionResponseParams(
      file.path(root_dir, "analysis", "7-sim-compare-freq_bs.qmd"), root_dir,
      response_manifest$params$simulation_seed, analysis_quick, analysis_dev, sim_size)
    .analysis_current_file(response_ctx, c("collated", "compare_raw.rds"),
      required_params = source_params)
    .analysis_current_file(response_ctx, c("collated", "compare_raw.rds"),
    required_params = c(list(comparison_semantics_version = source_params$comparison_semantics_version),
      analysis_result_params[c("stimgate_bias_uns_factor", "prob_exact", "cov_ev_min", "cov_ev_max",
        "n_sample_sim", "n_iter_sim", "stimgate_bw_mtd", "stimgate_bw_scope",
        "stimgate_bw_ncell_max", "stimgate_bw_ncell_min", "stimgate_bw_fallback",
        "stimgate_bw_min", "stimgate_bw_max", "cluster_gates",
        "loc_enforce_shape_threshold", "stimgate_loc_threshold_method", "calc_cyt_pos_gates",
        "fbeta_beta", "fbeta_theta", "fbeta_width", "tailgate_adjust", "tailgate_method",
        "tailgate_tol", "tailgate_auto_tol", "tailgate_bias", "tailgate_x")]))
  },
    error = function(e) { cat("Analysis 7 ROC comparison unavailable: ", conditionMessage(e), "\n\n"); NULL })
  if (!is.null(response_cache)) {
    response_scores <- .simCompareFisherScores(.analysis_read_rds(response_cache,
      response_ctx$analysis_key, response_ctx$qmd_path))
    roc <- .simCompareDetectionRoc(null_scores, response_scores, mcse = show_mcse)
    .analysis_report_table(roc$audit, c(fig_key, "roc-scenario-matching.csv"),
      "Explicit matched and unmatched genuine-response scenarios.", path_root = root_dir)
    if (!nrow(roc$curves)) {
      cat("No biologically matched null/response scenarios in these cache profiles.\n\n")
    } else {
      .analysis_report_table(roc$curves, c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "roc-curves.csv"),
        "Matched detection sensitivity and empirical FPR, with separate coverage.", path_root = root_dir)
      .analysis_report_table(roc$at_5, c(fig_key, paste0("mcse_", mcse_mode), "roc-supported-005.csv"),
        "Supported operating thresholds at or below 5% FPR; no interpolation.", path_root = root_dir)
      for (sep in unique(roc$curves$mean_pos_setting)) {
        for (prob in unique(roc$curves$prob_response)) {
          .analysis_heading(paste(sep, "separation; response", .analysis_label_percent(prob)), 3L)
          d <- dplyr::filter(roc$curves, mean_pos_setting == sep, prob_response == prob,
            method %in% fig_methods)
          if (!nrow(d)) next
          .analysis_print_save_fig(.simCompareDetectionRocPlot(d),
            file.path(plot_dir, "roc", paste0("roc_", sep, "_response_", prob, ".png")),
            mcse_mode = mcse_mode, fit_panels = TRUE)
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
